newsitem.title: CANADA: Newbridge sees market share aided by UB.
newsitem.headline: Newbridge sees market share aided by UB.

text.p: Newbridge Networks Corp garnered an important slice of the growing computer networking business with the acquisition of UB Networks from Tandem Computers Inc, company president Peter Charbonneau said on Thursday.

Newbridge announced it was acquiring UB Networks for undisclosed terms in a deal that was expected to close in late January. In mid afternoon trading, Newbridge was unchanged at C$40.40 on the Toronto Stock Exchange.

"They have a very complementary product line," Charbonneau told Reuters in an interview. Charbonneau, formerly executive vice president and chief financial officer, was named to the position of president and chief operating officer today.

Charbonneau said the acquisition positions the company well in the Internet and corporate "intranet" networking markets. He said UB Networks, which will be operated as a subsidiary, offers networking products that connect desktop computers to the communication routers and to the wide area network -- Newbridge's traditional strong suit.
"Now we have an end-to-end solution," said Charbonneau.
UB Networks with its 1,000 employees and US$380 million in annual revenue will account for about one-third of Newbridge's revenue base going forward, according to Charbonneau.

The computer networking market has been experiencing strong growth and Charbonneau saw it only continuing with continued demand for the link-up of personal computers and the rise of Internet-based communications.
"I think the marketplace is very, very strong," said Charbonneau.
